title: David Ellison Announces Skydance Leadership for New Paramount‑Warner Bros. Empire Deal
body:
The media landscape will shift dramatically next week as Skydance Media’s founder David Ellison revealed the senior leadership team that will steer the newly merged Paramount Global and Warner Bros. Discovery empire. The roster blends seasoned Warner Bros. Discovery executives with top brass from Paramount’s film and television divisions, signalling a strategic intent to fuse the two studios’ complementary strengths while preserving key talent from both sides.

Ellison’s announcement placed veteran Warner Bros. Discovery executives Mark Thompson, Casey Bloys and JB Perrette at the core of the new C‑suite. Thompson, who has overseen the company’s global distribution and streaming operations, will serve as chief executive officer of the combined entity, tasked with harmonising divergent corporate cultures and guiding the conglomerate through an increasingly fragmented entertainment market. Bloys, the longtime head of HBO and HBO Max, will assume the role of chief content officer, bringing his deep expertise in premium scripted series and a proven track record of building subscriber‑driven platforms. Perrette, formerly the chief financial officer of Warner Bros. Discovery, will take the helm as chief financial officer, charged with integrating the two companies’ balance sheets and delivering the cost synergies projected at $2 billion annually.

Joining the Warner‑derived leadership are Paramount’s film chief Dana Goldberg and senior vice president of original programming Josh Greenstein, who will oversee the combined film slate and television production respectively. Goldberg, known for shepherding blockbuster franchises such as “Mission: Impossible” and “Transformers,” will be tasked with aligning the newly expanded film portfolio, which now includes Warner’s storied properties like “Harry Potter” and “DC.” Greenstein, who has driven the growth of Paramount+ original content, will be responsible for unifying the streaming strategies of both legacy platforms—Paramount+ and HBO Max—into a single, globally competitive service.

The inclusion of George Cheeks, a veteran television executive with a background in both network and streaming development, rounds out the leadership team as chief operating officer. Cheeks will oversee day‑to‑day operations across the merged studio’s sprawling production pipelines, from scripted dramas to reality programming, ensuring that the combined entity can capitalize on economies of scale while maintaining creative agility.

Industry analysts view the composition of the new C‑suite as a pragmatic compromise. By retaining high‑profile Warner talent, Ellison signals respect for the company’s institutional knowledge and a desire to avoid the talent drain that often follows mega‑mergers. At the same time, the infusion of Paramount’s film and TV leaders reflects an ambition to leverage the studio’s recent successes in franchise building and streaming growth. “This blend of leadership is designed to create a unified vision without erasing the distinct identities that have made both companies successful,” said media consultant Laura Chen of StratEdge Research.

The merger, valued at roughly $30 billion, is expected to close on Tuesday, pending regulatory approval. If successful, the combined company will control an unprecedented catalog of intellectual property, ranging from Warner’s DC Universe and HBO’s prestige dramas to Paramount’s “Star Trek” and “Mission: Impossible” franchises. The new leadership will face immediate challenges, including integrating disparate technology platforms, reconciling divergent corporate cultures, and navigating antitrust scrutiny in the United States and Europe.

Looking ahead, the merged studio’s ability to deliver compelling content across multiple distribution channels will be the ultimate test of the new C‑suite’s effectiveness. With streaming competition intensifying and advertisers demanding innovative formats, the leadership team’s strategic choices will shape the future of Hollywood’s biggest conglomerate. As the deal finalises, stakeholders will be watching closely to see whether the combined Paramount‑Warner entity can fulfil its promise of a more powerful, yet cohesive, entertainment powerhouse.
